Chronic" non-ketonurica diabetes mellitus has an inhibitory effect on PGI(2) synthesis by the aorta, but an enhanced effect on the bladder.

Untreated diabetes mellitus has a biphasic effect on prostacyclin production by the aortic and urinary bladder vasculature of rats: acute (two days) ketotic and non-ketonemic (7 days) diabetes have no effect, whereas "chronic" non-ketonemic diabetes (62 days) causes a marked decrease in aortic PGI 2 production and a marked increase in PGI2 synthesis and excretion by the bladder.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of streptozocotin-induced diabetes on prostacyclin synthesis in the urinary bladder.
the effects of streptozocin-induced diabetes in rats on PGI2 (prostaglandin I2) synthesis by the rat urinary bladder.
the effects of diabetes mellitus on the synthesis and release of PGI2 by the rat bladder.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of diabetes mellitus on PGI2 is variable, tissue dependent and dependent on the duration and severity of the disease.

the bladder wall is a site where diabetes-induced changes in PGI 2 production may be observed, and that these changes are probably due to distension and/or hypertrophy of the organ, rather than to the diabetes mellitus per se. diabetes mellitus has a biphasic effect on PGI synthetase activity.

the effect of diabetes on PGI 2 production is dependent on the severity, duration and type of diabetes, and the tissue studied.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PGI2 production may be enhanced by bladder distension and hypertrophic changes.
the bladder is a major source of PGI2, and that PGI2 production in the bladder is affected by diabetes.
